blocker.summary: r458 investigated r457's 'MSAA render targets are not qualified this cycle' rejection and confirmed it is a genuine coverage gap, not a decode bug. A local diagnostic trace (AC6_NATIVE_VD_TRACE-gated, not committed) on derive_edram_render_target() showed RB_SURFACE_INFO=0x0a020280 -> msaa_bits=2, a real Xenos 4x-MSAA encoding, not a corrupted register value -- the game genuinely requests a multisampled EDRAM render target at this point. This corrects r457's prediction (which guessed this would likely be another quick targeted fix, same pattern as its own rect-list fix): PinnedShaderRuntime simply does not yet know how to create/resolve a multisampled EDRAM render target -- a real rendering-engine feature (multisample Vulkan image + resolve pass), not a one-line bug fix. Not implemented this cycle -- scoping it is out of scope for an investigation cycle. ctest 11/11, no regression. Named for r459: (1) scope and implement 4x-MSAA EDRAM render target support in PinnedShaderRuntime -- real engine work, likely its own dedicated cycle or several; (2) the first rejection reason characterized by r456 (pinned registry coverage) likely needs an oracle session -- user decision, not to be spent unilaterally. Still open, non-blocking: once the wiring is judged mature, reconsider the backlog commit decision (r433/r434/r438/r454-r458); update tools/prepare.py/build.py to default to the current ISO path (r452/r453, convenience only).
